name: Generalization of Empirical Learning

generalization.signal: No real comparable outcomes are currently available. NØX must not generalize from selection scores, predictions or expectations.

rules: Never generalize from a prediction alone.
Never generalize from an action-selection score.
Never generalize from a single outcome.
Only compare observations that are meaningfully comparable.
Keep context attached to every empirical pattern.
Separate repeated evidence from isolated events.
Preserve uncertainty when evidence is insufficient.
Do not treat correlation as guaranteed causation.
Do not generalize beyond the evidence available.

context_awareness.principle: An action that works in one context must not automatically be considered effective in every context.

decision_learning.future_use: Use validated empirical patterns as one evidence source when evaluating future action candidates.

confidence_update.reason: ACT43 identifies generalizable patterns but does not independently recalibrate confidence.

cognitive_learning.capability: Determine whether empirical action learning contains repeated patterns that can cautiously apply beyond the original observation.
cognitive_learning.what_nox_learned: A useful result becomes more informative when comparable results repeat in similar contexts, but one observation is not enough to establish a general rule.
cognitive_learning.future_use: Use validated patterns to improve future action evaluation while preserving context and uncertainty.

generalization_limits.conflicting_results_rule: Do not generalize until the conflict is understood.
generalization_limits.weak_evidence_rule: Keep the pattern as a hypothesis, not a rule.

next_action: Accumulate additional comparable real outcomes and test whether observed action patterns remain stable across contexts.
next_cognitive_step: ACT44 should detect when a previously effective strategy stops being effective or when empirical evidence becomes inconsistent.
